examples.ko: 계산이 끝나면 꼭 검산을 해 보세요.
examples.en: When you finish calculating, be sure to check your work.

examples.ko: 시험 시간이 남으면 검산이라도 한 번 더 하세요.
examples.en: If you have time left in the exam, at least check your calculations once more.

examples.ko: 검산은 다른 방법으로 풀어 보는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to check by solving it a different way.

examples.ko: 검산에 시간이 오래 걸려서 마지막 문제를 못 풀었어요.
examples.en: Checking took so long that I couldn't solve the last problem.

examples.ko: 다시 해 봤는데 검산이 맞아서 안심했어요.
examples.en: I tried it again and the check came out right, so I felt relieved.
In the accounting team, checking the figures is an important job too.

explain: '검산을 하다', '검산해 보다'처럼 써요. 글이나 서류를 다시 보는 '확인'과 달리 숫자 계산이 맞는지 따져 볼 때만 써요.
explain_en: It is used as '검산을 하다' or '검산해 보다'. Unlike the general '확인', it is only for checking whether a numerical calculation is right.

examples.en: We take turns driving every two hours.
I swapped shifts with the night worker in the morning.
The nurses will rotate every eight hours.
If you are too tired, would you switch with me?
At shift change, we do a handover.

examples.ko: 교대하고 나서 집에 가서 푹 잤어요.
examples.en: After the shift change, I went home and slept well.

explain: 일이나 운전을 사람이 번갈아 맡을 때 써요. 근무 시간표에서는 '3교대'처럼 숫자와 함께 나오고, '교대로'는 부사로 써요. 일상에서 가볍게는 '번갈아 하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Use it when people take turns at work or driving. In work schedules it appears with a number, as in '3교대' (three shifts), and '교대로' is the adverb form. In casual speech, '번갈아 하다' is also used.

en: written answer (on an exam); model answer

examples.en: The teacher showed us a model answer.
I forgot to write my name on the answer sheet.

examples.ko: 시간이 모자라서 답안을 끝까지 쓰지 못했어요.
examples.en: I ran out of time and couldn't finish writing my answers.

examples.ko: 채점할 때 학생 답안과 정답을 하나씩 비교해요.
examples.en: When grading, we compare each student's answer with the correct answer one by one.

examples.ko: 제 답안이 틀렸는지 다시 확인해 봤어요.
examples.en: I checked again to see whether my answer was wrong.

examples.ko: 답안을 제출하기 전에 한 번 더 확인하세요.
examples.en: Check once more before you hand in your answers.

explain: '정답'은 맞는 답이고, '답안'은 학생이 시험에 쓴 답이나 모범으로 보여 주는 답을 말해요. 그래서 틀린 답도 '답안'이라고 할 수 있어요. 답을 적는 종이는 '답안지'라고 해요.
explain_en: '정답' is the correct answer, while '답안' is the answer a student writes on a test or a model answer shown as an example. So even a wrong response can be called a '답안'. The paper you write answers on is the '답안지'.

examples.en: I won't be attending this gathering.
Many people were absent from yesterday's meeting.
I skipped the event because I wasn't feeling well.

examples.ko: 친구는 일 때문에 결혼식에 불참할 거예요.
examples.en: My friend will miss the wedding because of work.
If you can't attend class, please let us know in advance.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 부상 때문에 경기에 불참하고 집에서 쉬어요.
examples.en: That player is sitting out the match because of an injury and resting at home.

explain: '참석하다'의 반대이고, 회의·행사·모임처럼 정해진 자리에 안 간다는 공식적인 느낌이 있어요. 가벼운 말로는 '안 가요', '못 가요'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of 참석하다 and sounds formal, used for meetings, events and gatherings. In casual speech people more often say 안 가요 or 못 가요.

examples.en: Please watch your child's changes attentively.
The clerk wrapped the clothes with great care.
He attentively took care of the guests' requests.
Thanks to the careful preparation, the presentation went well.
Thank you for reviewing the manuscript so carefully.

examples.ko: 친구가 선물을 세심히 고르는 모습이 고마웠어요.
examples.en: I was grateful to see my friend choosing the gift with such care.

explain: '꼼꼼히'가 빠뜨리지 않는 것이라면 '세심히'는 상대를 배려하는 마음이 담긴 주의 깊음에 가까워요. 그래서 살피다·챙기다·배려하다 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: If '꼼꼼히' is about not missing anything, '세심히' is closer to attentiveness that carries consideration for others. That is why it goes well with verbs such as 살피다, 챙기다 and 배려하다.

examples.en: I called, but nobody answered.
Thank you for responding to the survey.
The customer center responded within ten minutes.
I like companies that respond to questions quickly.

examples.ko: 설문에 응답한 사람은 모두 이백 명이에요.
examples.en: Two hundred people responded to the survey in all.
To reply to an email, you must read it first.

explain: '대답하다'는 사람의 말에 직접 답할 때 쓰고, '응답하다'는 설문, 전화, 이메일, 서버처럼 요청이나 부름에 반응할 때 써요. 친구가 말을 걸 때는 '대답해요'가 자연스러워요. 컴퓨터가 멈추면 '응답 없음'이라고 떠요.
explain_en: '대답하다' is for answering what someone says directly; '응답하다' is for reacting to a request or call, such as a survey, phone call, email, or server. When a friend speaks to you, '대답해요' is natural. A frozen computer shows '응답 없음'.

examples.ko: 퇴사하기 전에 후임자에게 업무를 인계해야 해요.
examples.en: Before leaving the company, you have to hand over your work to your successor.

examples.ko: 정년을 앞둔 선배가 후배들에게 일을 인계하고 있어요.
examples.en: A senior colleague nearing retirement is handing his work over to the juniors.

examples.ko: 담당자가 바뀌어서 자료를 새 팀장에게 인계했어요.
examples.en: The person in charge changed, so I handed the materials over to the new team leader.
You can just hand the key over to the building manager.

examples.ko: 업무를 인계할 때는 문서로 정리해 두는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When handing over work, it's good to organize it in a document.

examples.ko: 일을 제대로 인계하지 않고 떠나서 팀이 힘들었어요.
examples.en: He left without handing over the work properly, so the team had a hard time.

explain: 맡고 있던 일이나 물건을 다른 사람에게 넘겨줄 때 쓰고, 받는 쪽은 '인수하다'예요. 두 말을 합친 '인수인계'를 회사에서 자주 말해요. 일상에서 가볍게는 '넘기다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when you pass a task or item you were responsible for to someone else, while the receiving side uses '인수하다'. The combined form '인수인계' is very common in workplaces. In casual speech people also say '넘기다'.

examples.en: The computer system suddenly stopped.

examples.ko: 은행 전산 오류 때문에 돈을 못 찾았어요.
examples.en: I could not withdraw money because of a bank system error.
Please ask the person in charge of IT.
My younger sibling studies computer science at university.
I entered the order into the system.
The hospital system was slow, so I waited a long time.

explain: '전산'은 회사, 은행, 병원에서 컴퓨터로 처리하는 일이나 그 시스템을 가리켜요. '전산 오류', '전산 입력'처럼 업무에서 자주 쓰는 말이고, 개인 컴퓨터 이야기에는 '컴퓨터'를 써요.
explain_en: 전산 refers to the computer-run side of work at companies, banks and hospitals, as in '전산 오류' or '전산 입력'. For talking about your own personal computer, just say '컴퓨터'.

examples.en: The photo was sent to my friend.
The file hasn't been sent yet.
Once the application is sent, an email arrives.
A message that has been sent can't be canceled.
The internet is slow, so the video transfers slowly.
All the data is being transmitted safely.

explain: 보내는 사람이 주어이면 '전송하다', 보낸 자료가 주어이면 '전송되다'예요. 사진, 파일, 메시지, 데이터를 보낼 때 써요. 택배는 '배송되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: When the sender is the subject use '전송하다'; when the sent item is the subject use '전송되다'. It is for photos, files, messages, and data. A parcel is '배송되다'.

examples.en: I printed out the meeting materials and handed them out.
I have to bring a printed-out plane ticket.
The printer broke, so I couldn't print.

examples.ko: 파일을 열어서 출력하는 방법을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please show me how to open the file and print it.

examples.ko: 흑백으로 출력하면 잉크를 아낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you print in black and white, you can save ink.
This program displays the result on the screen.

explain: 말할 때는 '프린트하다', '뽑다'가 아주 흔해서 '서류 좀 뽑아 주세요'라고 해요. '출력하다'는 조금 딱딱하고, 컴퓨터가 결과를 화면에 내보낼 때도 써요. 반대로 넣는 건 '입력하다'예요.
explain_en: In speech '프린트하다' and '뽑다' are very common, as in '서류 좀 뽑아 주세요'. '출력하다' is a bit stiffer and also covers a computer displaying results. The opposite is '입력하다'.

en: always; all the time; at all times

examples.ko: 이곳은 항시 열려 있어서 언제든 올 수 있어요.
examples.en: This place is open at all times, so you can come anytime.

examples.ko: 응급 상황에 대비해 항시 연락이 되게 해 주세요.
examples.en: Please make sure you can be reached at all times in case of an emergency.

examples.ko: 소방관들은 항시 출동할 준비를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: Firefighters are always ready to be dispatched.

examples.ko: 그는 항시 웃는 얼굴로 사람들을 대해요.
examples.en: He always treats people with a smiling face.

examples.ko: 이 약은 항시 가지고 다녀야 해요.
examples.en: You must carry this medicine with you at all times.

examples.ko: 문제가 생기면 항시 저에게 말씀해 주세요.
examples.en: If a problem comes up, please always tell me.

explain: '언제나, 늘'과 비슷하지만 '항시'는 안내문이나 공지, 뉴스처럼 딱딱한 글에 어울려요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '항상'이나 '늘'이 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is close to '언제나' and '늘', but '항시' fits stiff writing like notices, announcements and news. When talking with friends, '항상' or '늘' sounds more natural.
